**F002-i3 finding 1 (high, correctness — same-segment disclaimer suppresses explicit claim): fixed, red/green with regression tests.** The blanket disclaimer-wins rule in `_segment_class` was split into two disclaimer strengths in `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/doc_drift.py`: NEGATING disclaimers ("not a dispatchable", "not dispatched", "cannot be dispatched") still beat claim vocabulary because their phrasing contains the claim word they negate, while STATUS disclaimers ("operator-only", "operator surfaces", "planned", etc.) now lose to claim vocabulary in the same segment — so "a shipped executor for planned workflows" and "a shipped executor available on operator surfaces" classify as claims and flag gemini. The third probe ("Gemini (operator-only) is a shipped executor.") needed a second change: in `_mention_excused` rule 3, a strong-boundary disclaimer no longer excuses a mention when the segment run past it (via new `_claim_continues_past`, skipping consecutive disclaimers) resumes with a claim — the parenthetical is then an interrupting annotation inside a claim clause, not that clause's verdict. The honest attributive form "Gemini (operator-only) also runs the CLI" stays excused because the clause resumes with neutral prose. All three auditor probes were added first as the parametrized `test_status_disclaimer_cannot_suppress_explicit_claim` (confirmed failing, then passing), module/function docstrings were updated to document
